aRecipes.sHint: Pointer/String conversion (Unicode compiler) - check the direction; see the Unicode refactor family.
Duplicate global definition - remove or rename the later one.

An argument could not be resolved on this line - almost always a knock-on from an undefined symbol, e.g. a legacy Type member (like tRect.left) accessed as a Struct. Fix that symbol (see the 4328 on the same line) and this clears with it.

A compiler-internal literal token is invalid - fall-out from a broken expression on this line, usually an undefined symbol or a legacy Type member accessed as a Struct. Fix the root symbol (see the 4328 here), not the literal.

Type-check error - review manually. Usually an undefined or removed global, or a legacy Type member accessed as a Struct (Type->Struct); occasionally a reserved FMAC name (iEntry/iExit/iValidate) used as a local. Check the flagged symbol and any 4328 on the same line.

Wrong number of arguments - check the number of arguments the call passes against the function's declared parameter list. Two classic causes. (1) An OLD MISMATCH surfacing: DataFlex 19.1 and earlier let an expression-form call pass extra arguments unchecked, so a call that has been quietly wrong for years first errors here - and often the arguments fit a near-miss SIBLING (SelectFolder vs SelectFolder2), which is the function the call was meant for. Rewrite against the sibling, preferably in the Get form: Get Name of hoObject args to dest. (2) A NAME COLLISION with the newer DataFlex: a workspace method called as Name(Self, args) is still legal syntax, but when the new release owns the same name the call resolves to ITS function and the count no longer fits. The colliding owner can be invisible to a workspace search: DF26's runtime owns Split (declared in no package), and install packages declare more - Pkg\cSelectFolderDialog.pkg declares a 2-parameter SelectFolder - while the Studio's global search does NOT search the install's Pkg folder; check there before concluding the name is unowned. For a collision on a workspace method the Get form binds back to it: Get Name args to dest. Either way: if the argument count happens to FIT the wrong function, the call compiles and quietly misbehaves - so check sibling calls of the same name too.
Function not legal at runtime / has moved - check the owning package.

Undefined symbol - a missing DB field/table, a legacy Type member accessed as a Struct (Type->Struct migration, e.g. tRect.left), a source typo, or a TYPE NAME used as a conversion function, which DF26 refuses: Handle(x), Pointer(x), Boolean(x), DateTime(x) and UChar(x) all become Cast(x, Type) - and there the message names the type's INTERNAL name (LONGPTR for Handle, ADDRESS for Pointer), so the symbol it complains about may appear nowhere in the source. Check the flagged LINE before hunting for a missing field.

Symbol already defined - the flagged name is declared twice. Against a newer DataFlex target the classic cause is a hand-declared Windows API struct/constant that the runtime packages now define themselves: delete the local copy (or keep it for old targets behind a version #IF). A duplicate External_Function belongs in an #IFNDEF get_FunctionName guard; if both definitions are in the workspace's code, remove or rename one.

Undefined class - the class name in RefClass/Create resolves to nothing (a missing Use, a definition-order issue, or a removed/renamed class). Fix in source (define or Use it, or remove the reference); not an automated refactor.

An @-suffixed global the compiler cannot resolve is SPLIT at the '@' (the companion 4328 error names the stem). Usually the PROGRAM still declares the old bare name while a modernized shared package reads the g-prefixed one - run RefactorBareGlobalsToGlobalVariable on the program source (.src), not on the file this error points at.

A table definition file (.fd) was not found - the table is missing from the filelist, or its .fd was never generated for this workspace. Regenerate the .fd files in the Studio (Database Explorer / Synchronize Data Dictionaries); every <TABLE>.<column> undefined-symbol error that follows is cascade from this one missing file.

Runtime error 14 at COMPILE time: the compiler evaluated a CONSTANT expression and could not turn a quoted string into a number (DF 19.1 deferred that coercion to runtime; DF 25 folds it while compiling). Typical shape: a quoted 'TABLE.COLUMN' string literal compared against a NUMERIC variable - sibling lines against STRING variables slip through silently. Decide what was MEANT: a column REFERENCE (drop the quotes) or a text comparison (make both sides strings) - and check the surrounding same-shaped lines while you are there.

A DataFlex MESSAGE - typically a Procedure; sql.pkg's SQLExecute is the classic - is called function-style inside an expression. DF 19.1 compiled that and resolved it at runtime; DF 25 rejects it, because a Procedure has no return value an expression can use. The call was usually MEANT for a similarly-named wrapper FUNCTION: check for a near-miss name (SQLExecute vs SQLExecuteX), and for a local or parameter SHADOWING the wrapper's name - often the reason the wrong name got written. Point the call at the intended function; if a local shadows its name, rename the local too.

The name this line defines already exists - the compiler's duplicate-name check (the |CI token in the message is the existing symbol's internal id; its name is not printed). When a class that compiled clean on the old release trips this on the new one, the newer DataFlex usually provides the name natively from its RUNTIME - no Pkg source declares it, so searching the install finds nothing (DF 25 owns cRegEx this way). Rename the workspace's class and its use sites, or migrate them to the native feature. A version guard around the block is only safe when nothing still uses the workspace's version on the new release - the native API usually differs, so surviving call sites would silently change behaviour.
Obsolete command - see the message for the specific command and its modern replacement.

Obsolete package - see the message for the specific action: many are replaced with a modern class (e.g. dftable.pkg -> cCJGrid/cCJDbGrid), some are inert here and can simply be removed (e.g. a desktop-only package inside a WebApp), and some still declare fully-supported functions (MapiDllCalls.pkg is obsolete yet carries ShellExecute) - never remove a Use without checking what the file uses from it.

This package is obsolete AND ignored by the compiler in this program (e.g. a desktop-only package like Windows.pkg inside a WebApp) - it has no effect here. Remove its Use line; there is no modern-class replacement (a deletion, not a swap).
Obsolete class - replace with the modern equivalent.

Legacy registry/profile command - migrate the WHOLE block (root + open + read/write + close) to the cRegistry class (Use cRegistry.pkg): OpenKey/CreateKey, ReadString/WriteString, ReadDWord/WriteDWord, CloseKey when done. If the code targets an .ini FILE (a foreign profile) rather than the registry, use the cIniFile class instead. The commands are stateful as a group - hand-migrate the block, not line by line.

Gosub jumps to a label INSIDE this routine, sharing all its locals. Modernize by extracting the label block into a Procedure/Function and replacing the Gosub with Send/Get (shared locals become parameters/ByRef). Mind fall-through into the label block and any Goto entanglement - semantic surgery, review manually.

This Return pairs with a Gosub (a subroutine return). Quick fix: rename it to Gosub_Return. Better: extract the subroutine into a Procedure and use Procedure_Return - see the 'Obsolete command: Gosub' rows in this file.

Legacy ErrorSystem class - the modern runtime installs its own error handling; custom logic belongs in an Error_Report override (or the cApplication error hooks). The old object can usually be removed. Hand-migrate.
Legacy HelpSystem class - replace with cHtmlHelp (Use cHtmlHelp.pkg) and CHM-based help, then re-wire the help-context calls. Hand-migrate.
Legacy MAPI mail class - no direct modern equivalent. Simple notification mail: a mailto: shell launch; full mail handling: an SMTP or web-mail API integration. Hand-migrate.
This global is obsolete - see the message for which one, and what the runtime offers instead.
